newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 17.

text.p: A third of New Zealand's district police commanders did not deserve their jobs, Deputy Commissioner Barry Matthews said on Wednesday. Page 1.
NZ First strategist Michael Laws announced his retirement from politics, saying he plans to write two books - a novel and a satirical expose of political life. Page 1.

Alliance ruled out supporting National either by abstaining or voting for it on confidence issues, but denies that means giving carte blanche to a Labour-NZ First coalition. Issuing a 20-page document outlining common policies between Labour, NZ First and the Alliance, leader Jim Anderton said his party would only support a centre-left minority government if its policies came close to the Alliance's own committments. Page 2.

Deputy Prime Minister Don McKinnon gave National's most overt nudge to NZ First so far on Wednesday, saying the message from voters on Saturday was "go right". That analysis "might serve as useful guidance to NZ First as they decide which way to jump", McKinnon said. Page 2.

United NZ's new leader Peter Dunne joined ACT NZ yesterday in calling for National to seek a confidence vote in Parliament so it could rule as a minority government. Even if a minority government took office, negotiations for a coalition could continue, Dunne said. Page 2.

Retiring Trade Negotiations Minister Philip Burdon said it would be "very unsatisfactory" if New Zealand sent a caretaker prime minister to crucial regional trade talks next month. The Asia Pacific Economic CO-operation forum is the occasion at which New Zealand's prime minister gets to met the United States president and hold one-on-one meetings with other presidents and prime ministers from the region. Page 2.
NZ First Maori MP Tukoroirangi Morgan has been told by supporters to back a coalition with Labour. Page 2.

A rash of wholesale electricity price spikes has led to a call for urgent action by an "appalled" Major Electricity Users Group. Group chairman Terrence Currie said price spikes of more than 50 cents a kilowatt hour had happened on eight of the last 16 days since the market started. Page 15.

Sovereign Financial Services intends to offer home mortgages with an interest rate at least 0.25 percent cheaper than bank or building societies. Earlier on Wednesday, Ergo, an AMP subsidiary, said it had cut its three-year fixed residential
lending rate and a range of farm lending rates. Page 15.
The brakes went on the strong rally in financial markets on Wednesday after the Reserve Bank warned against taking interest rates too low. Page 15.
Natural Gas Corporation expects record gas sales of more than 50 petajoules this financial year, according to chief executive Richard Bentley. Page 15.
